one_liner: Senior Executive deputy running a 76-person Army G-8 directorate that builds the Army's multi-year budget program (POM/PPBE) across personnel, training, installations, logistics and IT.
fit_summary: This SES job requires executive leadership of large organizations and Army programming (POM/PPBE) expertise. Daniel's resume has neither, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public and requires U.S. citizenship; federal status and veterans' preference are not needed.

You must show all five Executive Core Qualifications and the MTQ, which is leading programming for a large, complex portfolio by aligning financial resources with Army strategic priorities. Both must appear within a strict two-page resume.
You must be able to obtain and keep a Top Secret clearance, and you must complete a background investigation and drug testing.
If selected, you must pass OPM's QRB structured interview on the ECQs. You must also file an OGE-278e financial disclosure and sign an SES mobility agreement.
strategy: Skip this one: it requires executive leadership of large organizations and Army programming (POM/PPBE) expertise, and his resume has neither.
Better-matched targets for building toward this kind of role are GS-9 to GS-12 program analyst, budget analyst or legislative affairs roles in Army, FEMA or DHS, or a Virginia VDEM position.
resume_bullets: Built Excel pivot-table reports on spending for multi-state COVID-19 purchasing (2021–2022).
Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance employees by organizing spreadsheets and analyzing the data for decision makers (2019–2020).
interview_questions: Describe a time you led the programming or budget process for a large, complex portfolio under fiscal uncertainty.
How have you held senior subordinates accountable while leading an organization through change?
Give an example of cutting waste or improving efficiency through process or technology changes.
How do you engage OMB, congressional staff, or other senior stakeholders to defend resource decisions?
watch_outs: This is an SES role, so the panel expects years of executive leadership and PPBE expertise. Daniel's known background is far below that bar.
A Top Secret clearance is required, along with background vetting.
The SES mobility agreement means you could be reassigned to other locations, and the job involves short-notice travel.
Any resume over two pages is immediately ineligible.
